articleTitle: PID Controller Design for Nonlinear Systems Based on Two-Time-Scale Motions
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: The paper treats in a tutorial manner a question of PI and PID controller design in the presence of plant's parameter variations and unknown external disturbances. The presented design methodology of PID control guarantees desired transients by inducing of two-time-scale motions in the closed-loop system. Stability conditions imposed on the fast and slow modes and sufficiently large mode separation rate between fast and slow modes can ensure that the full-order closed-loop nonlinear system achieves the desired properties in such a way that the transient performances are desired and insensitive to external disturbances and plant's parameter variations. The method of singular perturbations is used throughout the paper.

publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: Registering electrocardiogram in three orthogonal leads is useful for heart pathology's specific diagnostics, especially under continuous monitoring. But the fullest information is contained only in whole eight standard leads. So, it's very likely to recover standard leads form three orthogonal leads. This work describes a recovering algorithm that was developed, and it's validity estimation.

articleTitle: The Investigation of Physical Mechanism of Transcapillary Exchange by Phase-Sensitive Laser Method
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: The processes of diffusion and filtration are slow, and therefore a full cycle of gas exchange and metabolism at the level of capillaries of the blood circulation system cannot be realized in such a short time. A special laser setup was created for noncontact, noninvasive investigation of microcirculation and transcapillary exchange in a living object. With the help of investigations by using this setup, a phenomenon unknown before, that of the formation of an acoustic field in the lumens of microvessels (arterioles, capillaries, and venules) was discovered. With the help of the laser method, we detected that the transverse motion of the walls of microvessels in the high-frequency range really takes place. The authors advanced the problem of active interaction of moving erythrocytes in microvessels with smooth muscle cells of their walls for the first time. In blood vessels, smooth muscle elements are packed spirally. We suggest that there exists a special mechanism of regulation of metabolic processes.

abstract: Digital audio compression allows the efficient storage and transmission of audio data. The many forms of audio compression techniques offer a range of encoder and decoder complexity, compressed audio quality, and differing amounts of data compression. The article presents brief survey two algorithm groups of audio signal compression which can conditionally be divided into algorithms working in temporary area, and algorithms, working in frequency area. Audio data compression algorithm based on time-frequency presentation of signal is offered.

articleTitle: Application of Feedback Linearization for Air Gap Flux Control of Induction Motor in the Field Weakening Region
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: In present paper feedback linearization approach for induction motor control in flux - weakening region is proposed. Steady state equations of rotor flux feedback linearization control (FLC) are used for selecting optimal air gap flux level permitting maximum torque operation in field - weakening region. By adjusting the base speed for the constant power operation according to the air gap flux level, the current limit and the voltage limit can be achieved. Preliminary simulation results are presented.

publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: Born corn is regenerative born formation with all specific elements and histological structure of born tissue. It has been developed after fracture in born regenerative region. The influence of pulse solid state laser radiation to human fibroblasts in vitro and to animals in vivo has been studied. At the result we concluded that power pulse laser radiation decreases of proliferative and biosynthetic fibroblast's activity. This laser radiation was successfully used for control of born corn forming in aesthetic rhinoplasty.

publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: The method of 3D harmonic electromagnetic fields modeling for solving tasks of magneto-telluric sounding (MTS) has been developed and realized. Nonregular parallelepiped and hexahedral elements have been used for the finite element approximation. For acceleration of calculation of the field from local near-surface heterogeneities the multilevel scheme of 3D field separation has been developed.

articleTitle: Four-Level Rectifier and Four-Level Inverter for Electric Drives
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: A four-level three-phase diode clamped inverter fed by a correspondingly adapted untypical three-phase rectifier with two typical transformers is presented. The four-level rectifier is formed by consecutive connection of three rectifiers under the circuit of Scott for the bi-phase orthogonal voltage received from corresponding windings of two three-phase transformers. The inverter is realized by 4,5 kV IGBT modules and provides a voltage of 6 kV (RMS) for a high power induction machine without transformer. The dependences of THD and THD of integral values of the output voltage are simulated and shown for simple variants of three-carriers PWM and SVM.

articleTitle: Simple Free-Space Method for Measurement of Dielectric Constant by Means of Diffractive Optics with New Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: The monitoring of the composition of materials is an important problem of applied spectroscopy using optical, infrared, microwave and THz wavelength bands. MM and THz waves ensure better spatial resolution than microwaves and they can be used for material testing in media that are opaque for optical and infrared radiation. Whenever dielectric components are used in MM and THz wavebands, a precise knowledge of the dielectric properties of the material is essential. The developments original setups for dielectric material probing simultaneously at several discrete wavelengths within the same local zone are described.

articleTitle: Design of Power Electronics Driven PMSM with Constant Torque by Special Magnetic Circuit and Permanent Magnet Configuration
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: Special and high efficiency variable speed drives use permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) and power electronics. New dispositions for PMSM with regard to a special magnetic circuit design and new shapes of permanent magnet configurations are investigated. In order to obtain a better rotation performance and to reduce the torque ripple we propose the power electronics current control in support of a variable air gap. A variable air gap is a reasonable counter-measure for reducing the risk of demagnetization in case of short circuits that may occur will, drive arrangements. Today's power semiconductor switches survive short circuits - PMSM generally do NOT. In this study the PMSM with radial flux distribution is used and magnet configurations are computed using two-dimensional finite element method magnetics (FEMM). PMSM design ideas are presented which exhibit constant torque and demagnetization risk reduction.

articleTitle: A Study of Input Current Model for New Multipulse Three-Level Rectifiers of Three-Phase Orthogonal Voltages Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: The simple approach has been used to estimate the input currents of the new multipulse three-level rectifiers of three-phase orthogonal voltages systems. Nine the rectifier schemes have been covered with a simulation. The crest factor, the distortion factor and the total harmonic distortion of the input current for the twelve-, fifteen-, twenty-four-, thirty- and forty-eight-pulsed rectifiers has been computed in Simulink-SimPowerSystems transformerless models. The integral factors of harmonics have been evaluated as functions of the angle of overlap for the 12-pulsed rectifier with the series output connection of the rectifier bridges.

articleTitle: Implementation of Rugged Measurement System on Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: Electrical vehicles are favorable alternatives for transport under special environmental conditions. For financial and availability reasons the vehicles are powered by lead-acid batteries as a standard. Low capacity and limited driving range are the consequence and require a range of estimation. This is to be realized on the basis of charging and energy consumption. That is influenced for instance by charging current and duration, temperature outside and at motor and at battery, battery voltage, losses in converter and machine, speed at driving, height difference, empty and payload of vehicle, possible recharging during standstill e.g. by included photovoltaic. Therefore, many signals are to be measured. A rugged measurement system running on traction battery is realized and prepared for a test on a Golf car vehicle with 4 kW power rating.

articleTitle: PID Controller Design for Nonlinear Systems Based on Two-Time-Scale Motions
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: The paper treats in a tutorial manner a question of PI and PID controller design in the presence of plant's parameter variations and unknown external disturbances. The presented design methodology of PID control guarantees desired transients by inducing of two-time-scale motions in the closed-loop system. Stability conditions imposed on the fast and slow modes and sufficiently large mode separation rate between fast and slow modes can ensure that the full-order closed-loop nonlinear system achieves the desired properties in such a way that the transient performances are desired and insensitive to external disturbances and plant's parameter variations. The method of singular perturbations is used throughout the paper.

articleTitle: Is it Possible to Make Materials with Ionic Superconductivity?
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: We try to find some materials in which bosonic ions with sufficiently small effective mass are used as charge carriers instead of Cooper's pairs in order to provide high temperature ionic superconductivity. Among single-charged ions comprising ionic crystals only lithium isotope Li6 can be used for that purpose. The results show that Bose-condensation temperature for Li6-ions is of the order of 10-34-10-43K in all crystals. If, however, the crystal is compressed by 20-22%, it can rise the Bose- condensation temperature in all crystals considered to above room temperature.

Numerical study of convergence of the mixed vector finite element method and the vector finite element method in three-dimensional case on class of problems, having known smooth analytical solution is performed. abstract: Our report examines use of healthcare information technologies. articleTitle: Advanced Finite Element Analysis for High Power Wind Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: In order to build light-weight wind power rotor blades it is necessary to design thin walled parts so that the weight of the rotor blade is no longer the limiting factor for the size of the plant. Up until now it has been necessary to use a complex three-dimensional calculation with the help of the finite elements method (FEM). In this thesis special finite line elements are introduced, with which the numerical determination of the shear stress distribution due to cross-sectional bending and torsion as well as important cross-sectional parameters, e.g. shear centre, shear and torsion stiffness of thin-walled beams (e.g. rotor blades) is possible. In order to calculate these parameters, only knowledge of the material properties and the cross-sectional geometry is necessary and not the longitudinal stretching of the rotor blade. This is possible because the three-dimensional problem can be transferred into a two-dimensional one.

articleTitle: Design Study of Power Electronics Fed Transversal Flux Machine in Axial Arrangement
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: The transversal-flux-machine (TFM) is a completely different design if compared to normal machines. Developed for generally low speed and high torque, e.g. driving vehicles without gear, the transvesal-flux-machine is a high-pole machine with simplified stator winding but on the other hand with an extremely complicated magnetic design. This causes many mechanical problems in the set up of such a machine. The few industrially manufactured models are of radial design like standard electrical machines. This paper investigates the possibilities and problems of an axial prototype of a transversal-flux-machine, considering a low power prototype for a variable speed drive.

articleTitle: Sectional Ultrasonic Irradiator for Intracavitary Treatment
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: In this paper experimental results on sectional ultrasonic irradiator (USI), which is implemented on several piezoplates located parallel to each other on lateral surface of cylindrical body, are presented. It is shown that with section number increase from 1 up to 4, uniformity of irradiation intensity across USI sharply increases. The further increase in number of sections increases the uniformity more poorly. It is noted, that six-section USI provides fluctuation of intensity across radiator only on 10-15 %.

articleTitle: Modular 3-Port Isolated Current- and Voltage Measurement System for Advanced Converter Control
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: Precise isolated current and voltage measurement is a frequent task in measurement and control. 3- port isolation simplifies assembling of the measurement system. Typical applications are multichannel data acquisition, ground loop elimination, motor control and rapid prototyping. High common-m.de rejection ratios because of high rate of rise of voltages at switching (high switching speed of state-of-the-art semiconductors have rise and fall times typically less than 1 mus) could be reached by avoiding capacitive cross-coupling. The output signals are scaled signals (+/-10 V or 5 V range) suited directly for A/D-converters. This paper describes the concept of 3-port isolation in current- and voltage a measurement system which is a prerequisite for advanced converter control.

articleTitle: The Quality of Ocular Artifacts Suppression in Electroencephalogram Depending on Selection of a Wavelet Mother Function for a Signal Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: The traditional method of the suppression of ocular artifacts is a cutting off the contaminated periods of EEG. The drawback of such a technique is a significant loss of the diagnostic information. The method of ocular artifact suppression in EEG, based on wavelet analysis, is investigated in this study. However different groups are proposing various combinations of wavelet mother functions, thresholds and so on, and each group achieves good results by their own method. Here we compare the efficiency of using different wavelet mother functions in the procedure of ocular artifacts suppression. By co-ordination of results in different estimation ways (some of them are cross-correlation, kurtosis and relative entropy by Shannon) we could conclude about efficiency of different wavelet basises and consistent of proposed ways of estimation. Results of investigation can be used as practical recommendations in developing of EEG de-noising algorithms.

articleTitle: A Bad Data Processing Algorithm for a Substation Automation System
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: This paper addresses a novel data error detection method in a substation. Unlike conventional methods, the proposed algorithm uses logical reasoning taking general structure of a substation into consideration. A substation model is divided into several modules according to the voltage level and connection status. For the analog data correction, the conservative reasoning is adopted, which means that a data value is not evaluated to be "true" unless every evidence is proved. For digital data, a measure "falseness" is suggested, by which a data can be evaluated to be false or not. Simulations on a standard substation of KEPCO demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: There are many well-known materials used in constructions, mechanical engineering, etc. which contains some periodical cavities and inclusions (e.g. sphere plastics). Stiff characteristics of equivalent homogeneous materials must good approximate such heterogeneous material properties. There are sufficient set of papers devoted to this problem the most extensively studied for two-dimensional bodies (2D stress state and 2D strain state). In present paper the method of effective characteristics determination for three-dimensional medium containing doubly periodic system of parallel cylindrical cavities is proposed.

articleTitle: The Gauss Wave Packets Scattering on the Regular Lattice of Finite Length
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: In this work we have studied in detail the one-dimensional scattering on the lattice formed by the row of N identical delta-barriers which is the one-dimension diffraction grating for electrons. The steady-state wave functions psi(E,x) and scattering amplitudes were found by the transfer-matrix method. The transmission factor T = T(E) spectrum consists of the alternating transparency and opacity zones. Inside of the transparency zones T(E) is modulated proportionally to the Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind so that there are N - 1 narrow spectral lines of full transmittivity in each zone. The amplitude of modulation increases considerably near the edges of zones where there are a few narrow spectral lines of full opacity too. In this lines of full opacity the steady-state wave functions have large resonant amplitudes inside the lattice.

articleTitle: Power Electronics Controlled DC Drive for Geophysical Earth Magnet Field Reversal Simulation
publicationTitle: 2006 8th International Conference on Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering
abstract: A power electronics fed DC motor is controlled on a given constant speed and drives a generator with both series and auxiliary external excitation. The induced voltage at generator yields a DC current caused by load resistor. That current also is the main source for generator excitation holding the generator in stable steady state operation in connection with hysteresis in magnetic circuit. If we apply a small current in the auxiliary external excitation of generator we produce either a filed-increasing or a field-decrceasing component in magnetic field. A constant small counter-excitation will reduce the field until it gets zero. If this small counter-excitation is present for all the time we will reverse the field and finally establish a field in counter direction. At opposite polarity of current and field we reach again a condition stabilized by magnetic saturation at the generator. The established system is small-scale model of earth magnetic field described by geodynamic generator. This implies the existence of enormous currents in the core of the earth which cause the magnetic field in the range of about 1 milliTesla on earth surface. The small external current in the model has its, equivalent in the stream of charged particles emitted by the sun. The effect of magnetic field reversal in the 1 kW - model can be viewed by several display units over some seconds rather than millions years in reality.

Author Keywords: simulation of earth magnetic field reversal

abstract: In the article a new physical mechanism of ventilation of the lungs based on the helical countercurrent motion of gas mediums in tracheobronchial tree is considered. Existence of the phenomenon of formation of a helical countercurrent motion of the gas mediums predicted theoretically, is proved experimentally. On the basis of morphometry of tracheobronchial tree and the theoretical analysis, partition and confluence of contrary helical streams in nodes of branching of aeriferous channels is considered. The obtained fundamental results have allowed to lay foundation of new technology of artificial ventilation of the lungs for anesthesiologias, reanimotologia and intensive care. In clinical conditions high efficiency and optimality of the suggested technology is achieved.
